_README: wa_liberty_bell_independence_route's approach described THE WRONG SIDE OF THE MOUNTAIN.
The row is aspect E and is an East Face line - the 1966 first ascent took the profusely
overhanging northeast corner, and it joins Thin Red Line at M&M Ledge. Its stored approach read
'Same as the Beckey Route: Blue Lake Trailhead ... 4th-class ledges across the West Face'. The
Beckey Route is the SOUTHWEST face. The text sent a party to a trailhead on the opposite side of
the peak, about 2.5 road miles away over Washington Pass.
Liberty Bell's own rows say so plainly: wa_liberty_crack records that the East Face approach
'does NOT start from the Blue Lake Trailhead - that's the trailhead for the west-side Beckey
Route', and wa_liberty_bell_east_face says the same.
The replacement is RE-HOMED, not composed. Sentences 1-3 are wa_liberty_bell_east_face's own
approach; sentence 4 is this route's position along that base, from its own researched
approach_variant (far right / north edge, under the red Baer Ceiling ~85 m up).
The old '2 miles and ~2,000-2,200 ft of gain' figures are DROPPED rather than converted - they
measure the Blue Lake approach to the other side, and no source gives an East Face equivalent

wa_liberty_bell_independence_route._why: approach walked to the West Face via Blue Lake Trailhead on an East Face route; re-homed from the East Face sibling row

set.approach: This is on the East Face, so — like Liberty Crack — the approach is not from the Blue Lake Trailhead but from a separate pullout on SR-20 at the hairpin curve just east of Washington Pass. Park on the north shoulder near the curve, walk back toward the pass to a small pond on the south side of the highway, round its east end, and follow a cairned boot path north into the forest. The path climbs through timber and breaks out onto the talus field directly below the East Face after roughly 20-30 minutes and 0.5 mile (~600-800 ft gain). From where the path reaches the talus, continue right (north) along the base past the Liberty Crack starts to the far right-hand end of the face, below the red Baer Ceiling roof about 85 m above. No water source along the way; watch for the cairned track being hard to follow in low light, and loose talus underfoot at the base.
